utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Pilipovic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is it the Defence ready to -- well, to call its next witness would not be the right wording, because he entered the courtroom already as far as I see. It's usually I think new witnesses wait outside until they are called. But it's not a disaster. Are you ready to... Then, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving evidence in this Court, Witness, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out, and may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to -- to ask you to give us your full name and surname and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: My name is Bukva Milorad, born on the 17th of January, 1958.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, can you tell us about your educational background and career.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Following the primary school, I went to the secondary military school. I completed two years in Zagreb and then two years in Belgrade after military school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just, Mr. Bukva, can you go slowly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. After that, I completed military academy in Belgrade. This was the communications section. And then following the war in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, I completed the general staff school in Belgrade. As far as my career is concerned, this started after I finished the military academy. And then I became engaged at the 351st communications platoon in Sarajevo. It was -- in September 1981 that I started my service in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, I understood from your answer that before the conflict broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, in Sarajevo, you had your service, you were doing your service in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me in 1981, when you started working at the 351st platoon, communications platoon, where was the base of your platoon? Where were you stationed? Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This platoon was in Sarajevo. The exact location is Slobodan Princip Seljo barracks. My initial duties, I carried out to start with, were to be a commander of the platoon, commander of the company. And then in 1986, I went to the service for intelligence and information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were located at the Slobodan Princip Seljo barracks in Sarajevo. Can you tell us what part of town is that so that we can be clear about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I think I said it was Lukavica. It's a suburban part of town, it was known as Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is not a platoon, it is regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bukva, considering that you told us your background, can you tell us in spring 1991 [sic], were you in service at the regiment of the intelligence and information department? Were you still working in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at that time, what was your rank? That is, in spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, I was captain first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your specialty, so from 1986, that is, and 1992, you were doing intelligence and information duties. Were you informed or did you have any knowledge about the situation in the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the withdrawal of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. And I believe that I was extremely well-informed about the situation at the barracks because we were already then under some kind of measures of heightened combat readiness, and we were always away of what could happen because there was a threat of an attack, as it did happen in -- when the war in Croatia started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Considering your answer, were there any particular measures that were taken so that this atmosphere of tension is somehow relieved?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a number of measures were taken. First of all, there were political activities that were very lively in order to calm down the situation which was not promising at all. On the contrary. But the other side, that is, the Muslims, whenever there was an agreement, the other side, the Muslims, betrayed it. They were -- they tricked us. They didn't follow the agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, considering that you told us that the army was in the barracks, and that the situation was very tense, the atmosphere was very tense, you personally, did you have information or data that certain units, and if so, which ones, have positions outside of the barracks? That is, in certain locations -- on certain locations outside of Sarajevo. Do you have such information?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: You mean the JNA?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still talking about 1992. I'm talking about the JNA. I'm talking about the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, this answer flows out of my previous answer. This is within the measures of calming the situation down. Specifically, we had certain orders that some movement of Yugoslav People's Army units be reduced as much as possible, in order not to irritate, in inverted commas, the local population. So practically speaking, we did not leave the barracks. So we cannot really speak about some units being on some positions outside of Sarajevo. That is completely untrue to state such a thing. So there's absolutely no question; the units were not at any positions. We were in the barracks. That was the permanent composition of the JNA, that is, the recruits of military schools and those serving their military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, on whose decision did it depended that the JNA was to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: That was a political question. A decision was supposed to be taken at the political level, while the army, in accordance with such a decision, was supposed to follow it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew with all the troops and all the equipment from Sarajevo, and if you know, when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, I can speak at length about this. But one of the conditions was that units that happened to be in the city, and those that were blocked by the forces of the then Patriotic League, the condition was that those units could leave with a proviso that they would leave the weapons in the barracks, leave the weapons behind. And in order to protect lives of those JNA members, that's how it was decided, and that's how this was conducted. Weapons were mostly left behind in the barracks. Partly some weapons were taken out of the barracks, and this was mostly infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you didn't just -- you didn't answer when was that. I asked you in my question when was it that the JNA withdrew with the equipment, and the troops. Was there a specific period, specific date, or did it go in stages?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I think that was 19th of May, I believe. I'm not absolutely certain, but that was in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your answers, and I believe that I followed you correctly, the JNA did not have any positions on important strategic positions in and around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They did not have any such positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether a number of officers of the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew, and if they did, how many of them did? Rather, was there a decision pertaining to the officers of the Yugoslav People's Army at the time when the Yugoslav People's Army was withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Most of the officers and noncommissioned officers withdrew together with the JNA into the territory of Yugoslavia, except for members who were born in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, they were allowed to stay there. However, before then, we were abandoned by all the -- or rather, the JNA was -- all the members of the Muslim nation left the JNA. For instance, my regiment had 120 officers and noncommissioned officers in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were another three noncommissioned officers who remained together with me. So perhaps, 4, 5 per cent. Probably 4 per cent officers and noncommissioned officers remained. I believe that was the situation in other units as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you tell us, when was the Army of Republika Srpska established including the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: The decision regarding the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska was adopted at the assembly session on the 12th of May. And the actual act of creating the army, the Army of Republika Srpska, also created the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally have any knowledge as to which units were part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and when was the Sarajevo Romanija Corps established?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: You cannot really speak about units that were part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. The Sarajevo Romanija Corps was established over a period of time, and it included with itself all those units that existed at the time, existing on the territorial principle, that is, on the principle of Territorial Defence. That is that Sarajevo Romanija Corps encompassed all those forces that were in existence on the field, on the ground. They didn't have any kind of names, so to speak, except that they were linked to topographic locations where they were on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was made up of units of the Territorial Defence which existed in certain areas, do you personally have knowledge as to what was the disposition of the Territorial Defence units in the area of the city of Sarajevo, and do you know in what way were certain areas taken by the units of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: The initial stages of the war, during that initial stage, the Serb population of that area had to self-organise, that is, they had to defend their own houses. They had to defend their own settlements, villages. And according to that principle, there was establishment of an informal front line. And to be more specific, the demarcation area, the demarcation line between the Muslim and the Serb population, followed the ethnic line, the ethnicity line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that these lines followed the ethnic line and that on the Serb side, there were units of the Territorial Defence, can you tell us did you know what was the situation in terms of organisation on the other side, on the side where the majority of the population were Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I'll try and be brief. During the war in Croatia, the Muslim authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina had already forbidden recruits to join the JNA. As far as their able-bodied men, that is, those of military eligible age, they were prevented from going to Croatia. So already in 1992, we can speak of an extremely well -- military force of Muslims that was active through the Party of Democratic Action. And as recruits went to join the JNA, and JNA was a very important guarantor of security for all three nations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, what was then understood by the Serb population was that war was coming. And looking at the way the Muslims were being militarily organised, that's how the units of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, if I may interrupt you, you and Ms. Pilipovic are speaking the same language. And since the -- you're both speaking quite quickly, could you please slow down so that the interpreters can translate all the words you speak. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what I wanted to add, I wanted to add another detail. The most extremist individuals in the Patriotic League were well-known Sarajevo criminals who were absolute terror of Sarajevo prior to the war. They were not just a terror of the Serbs, but also of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, when you told us that the establishment of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was a longer process and that it encompassed units of the Territorial Defence which were in some areas of the city where there was a majority Serb population, can you tell us whether according to you these positions of the territorial army -- Territorial Defence units, whether this was somehow being controlled by the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this position of these units, according to the ethnic principle on both sides, did it somehow reflect the situation in the city of Sarajevo, and if so, when was this possible to notice?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have already explained. When the JNA left, people felt very insecure, and there was immediately movement of population. That is, in those areas where there was majority population of Serbs, the Muslims left that part of town to those parts of town where there was majority population were Muslims and the other way around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bukva, when the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was established, and we will be speaking about September 1992, and if you have any information or knowledge before September 1992, did you attend meetings at the corps command during this period, that is, at the time when the corps was established?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, it seems that I didn't answer one part of the question. The establishment of the corps was a process which lasted for a certain period of time. You can say that it ended at the end of 1992. I was a member of the corps command, and I attended a number of meetings. And in the role as officer for intelligence duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go back to your duties as officer for intelligence and security matters, as officer of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. But my question now is whether -- would you be informed about the objective, that is, was there a war objective in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in relation to Sarajevo? Was there some talk of this, and whether you can tell us about the positions in the corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Most of the members of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and most of the command personnel, they knew what the war objective of the SRK was. It was defined by the assembly decision which practically confirmed the situation on the ground which was the division of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say the actual situation on the ground and the division of the city. Are you referring to the lines that were established between the Territorial Defence on the Serbian side and members of the organised Muslims units on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, was that the objective that had been set?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, and I'd like to repeat that that was the decision taken by the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when the Republika Srpska army started functioning as an army and was under a single command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, it started functioning as an army when they declared the existence of the Army of Republika Srpska. During a certain period of time, it had certain problems which were overcome as in the course of their duties. But you could say that it had all the characteristic of an organised and functional army by the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that it had certain problems when it was formed. Can you tell us what sort of problems it encountered when the Republika Srpska army was formed and the SRK, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. One of the main, most persistent problems, was the lack of qualified and -- the lack of qualified professional officers. A while ago, I mentioned my JNA unit which left Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I said that the situation was more or less the same in other units. There were very few qualified commanding officers so that there were commands at lower levels which lacked such men. And this was a serious problem. Secondly, it was difficult for us to bring units up to strength because there were very few Serbs in comparison to the enemy. And thirdly, we had certain problems in relation to putting certain groups and units under control, certain groups and units which we considered to be paramilitary groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned the problems that appeared while the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was being formed. Can you tell us whether during that period, and with regard to those noticeable problems, were any measures taken in order to solve these problems? How long did this take, and in your opinion, was that problem solved at a given moment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, as I have already said, it's very -- forming an army is a very difficult and lengthy process. The problems that we encountered were successfully solved as rapidly as possible because the situation was such that this was necessary. In our opinion, we eliminated all of those problems, and as I have already said, we managed to organise a functional army by the end of 1992. Certain problems which concerned paramilitary units were also very rapidly solved at the very beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you solved the problems that you had within the corps. Can you now tell us who issued orders according to which problems would be solved within the corps, problems concerning both paramilitary units and discipline and all the other problems that you mentioned, that you have mentioned, and which existed in the corps? Who issued such orders?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: We received the orders of this kind from the superior command, that is to say, from the main staff, on the basis of those orders and of what was necessary, the corps command would also issue its own orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that there were paramilitary units. Before I put a certain series of questions to you with regard to solving the problem of paramilitary units, could you tell us exactly what your duties covered as an intelligence officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I'll try and be brief. When the SRK was formed, as one of the elements of command, there was also a section for intelligence and security affairs. And it consisted of two parts, two departments: A department for intelligence and a security department. I was the chief of the intelligence department. The task of that department was to ensure that all the conditions for carrying out intelligence and security within the corps existed. That meant that it was the task of my department to provide the command with a sufficient amount of quality information on the enemy in order to avoid surprises of any kind. That meant that it was necessary to know the strength of the enemy, the number of men, the state of morale, the deployment of forces, the kind of weapons it had, the training they had, their objectives, purposes, activities, and all other information that would indicate what the nature of the enemy was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described in more detail your department. Can you tell us who they reported to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: As the chief of that department, I was subordinated to the chief of the corps staff. And in professional terms, I was subordinated to the chief of the department for intelligence and security affairs in the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As chief of the intelligence department, who did you relay intelligence to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: To the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will later return to the issue of receiving and gathering intelligence on the enemy. But I would now like to turn to the issue of paramilitary units, the problem of paramilitary units that existed when the SRK was formed. Can you tell us how you solved the problem of paramilitary units in that area? Could you first tell us, if possible, what paramilitary units are?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, paramilitary units are groups of people who are not subordinated to anyone in particular. They don't respect commands, superior commands, and they quite simply behave and act outside the law that governs armies. The problem of paramilitary units or groups or individuals was solved above all via political means. This means that the organs of power played an essential role in putting those units under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. And the results were very good. Most of these units were thus placed under the control of the army of Republika Srpska, that is to say, under the control of the SRK. A negligible number refused to be placed under the control of the army, and we solved this problem in the way provided for by the law, and that is by having recourse to force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that -- now that you've told us how you solved the problems that related to the paramilitary units, and we've heard quite a lot of testimony about certain units that were in the area of the SRK, can you tell us which paramilitary units you had problems with and were, so to speak, subordinated to the corps command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, a characteristic example would be a certain group which called itself Chetniks. It existed in Ilidza, and in spite of all the attempts that were made to "peacefully" place them under the command of the SRK, the military police units had to intervene to disarm that group and its members, and we had to mobilise the members and place them in other units so that they would no longer form a single unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question as to whether you know and will remember which units are concerned. You mentioned the Chetnik unit in Ilidza. But were there such units in other areas, too? And I am referring to paramilitary units. When you solved these problems, when you were solving these problems, who did you cooperate with closely when solving those problems in certain areas where those units were located?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: All I said is that -- all I told you about was a drastic example, and in this case, we were forced to have recourse to force. But as I have already said, most of those units were placed under control through political means, through carrying out -- through working in the field. I think that there was a group Gedora. I think that was the name. But I don't think there were any other cases in which we had to use force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that your department and you, as the chief of the intelligence department, had some duties. You told us which duties it had to perform and what sort of information it had to gather. My question is as follows: On the basis of that intelligence, do you remember what sort of -- what kind of men and weapons the BH army had, and if you do, on the basis of what kind of information did you receive such intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: As I have already said, I've already mentioned one of the ways that the military part of the Party of Democratic Action used to arm. Its members would go to the war in Croatia, and they would return with weapons. At the beginning of the war, these weapons were quite sufficient for the Patriotic League and its members to enable them to launch certain armed attacks against former JNA barracks. And this is how they managed to obtain a certain amount of weapons. The third way of obtaining weapons was through an agreement that had been reached about withdrawing from the barracks of the former JNA in Sarajevo. The Muslims demanded a third of the weapons of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I personally was present when the Muslims were given certain infantry weapons when withdrawing from the Viktor Bubanj barracks. This was from the Territorial Defence warehouse. I'm not sure what the amount was, but I think it was about 3.500 guns. The fourth way of obtaining weapons by the Muslims is the one I have already described. When the JNA units were leaving the barracks in Sarajevo, and this was all just before the beginning of war. That's when all of this happened. And so it's possible to conclude that they had quite good infantry weapons and also anti-armour weapons. As far as the men were concerned, throughout the war, we were in an inferior position, and it's possible to say that throughout the war, the ratio was 1 to 4 in favour of the Muslims. 1 to 4 or 1 to 3.5, or rather 1 to 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you have said how the BH army obtained weapons, and the extent to which it was armed, and you have also said how many men they had, you said 1 to 4 or 1 to 3.5, do you know how many men the BH army had? That is to say, the BH army corps in the period of 1992, 1993, and 1994, and how many men did the Sarajevo Romanija Corps have?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, that can be determined quite precisely. And as I say, on the basis of the information that we had, in Sarajevo itself, in the city of Sarajevo, in the part of the town that was under Muslim control, the enemy had about 35 to 38.000 armed men. But the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, when it was at maximum strength, I think it had, as far as I can remember, about -- between 18 and 20.000 men. But there's something that's specific to the SRK, and that is the fact that it was in a semi-encirclement. It was what we called an outer ring, and it linked up about 40.000 enemy soldiers. So on the whole, the total number of enemy forces was about 78.000, whereas our corps had between 18 and 20.000 men at the most. And later on, as the war advanced, the number of men diminished because of the casualties suffered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, you told us that you had information according to which the part of town which was under BH army control. In that part of town, there were between 35 and 38.000 armed troops. In 1992 and 1993, up until August 1994, did you have any information on the positions of the weapons that the enemy side had? Did you have any information according -- telling you where the soldiers of the 1st Corps were located in that part of the town, and if you did have any such information, how did you obtain it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, all intelligence services have several means of obtaining information on the army. We mostly got our best information through conversations with people who had come from other parts, had crossed over from the territory of the part of the town that was under Muslim control. Naturally, there were other ways of obtaining information on the enemy. We had a very good network at the front line itself which carefully monitored all enemy moves and observed the enemy. And by observing the enemy, we were able to obtain very reliable information on the enemy. Naturally, we had a certain amount of information that was obtained through monitoring the media. We received very reliable information through monitoring the enemy's radio links and other communications. We took advantage of the weaknesses that their communication system had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, you have told us how you obtained information on the enemy deployment, on the enemy positions, and on where the men and weapons were located. Did you have any information for the period that we are interested in according to which there were workshops in that part of town where weapons were being produced? And if you did have such information, what was the source of the information? Or if it was the same source, it's not necessary to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, we think that we had very good information, very reliable information, on the workshops where the weapons were produced because we thought this was important. It was important for our command to have such information. On the whole, we obtained this information through conversations with people who had crossed over and who in a certain sense had contact with those sites. They were either in a work platoon or they had been captured or something like that. In any event, they knew about those locations, and we managed to determine that this information was correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bukva, if the Defence shows you a map, given what you can remember and the information that you disposed of, would you be able to indicate the positions on that map which you knew to be positions where the army was located and where there were workshops and areas in which there were weapons used by the BH army in the period that the Defence is interested in, September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, to an extent I think I could do so, although I may have forgotten certain things.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence would like to show a map of the town of Sarajevo. It does the one that we have used up until now. I have marked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all have the experience that marking in Court takes a tremendous amount of time. Would it be a suggestion that we would ask the witness to do some of the marking during the break under the supervision of the parties, and that you then ask questions about it? Not the break to be now, but to move to another subject first unless it would interfere in such a way with your line of questioning that we could not wait for another half an hour. But since it's on my list that you asked for four hours to examine the witness, perhaps there would be another subject that could be dealt with first, and we would then ask the witness to mark. But I would like you then to instruct the witness quite clearly just before the break on how the markings should be made because you're asking for several kind of locations. I noticed that you asked for workshops and you also asked for positions where the army was located. I don't know whether half an hour would be sufficient to mark all the positions where the army was located. But if you would please give the witness precise instructions just before the break how to mark it and what exactly to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you please tell us during the relevant period of time where was your post, your working position? Which facility did you occupy where you carried out your duties?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: My section for intelligence tasks was as part of the department for the security intelligence matters of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and those two sections, departments, were located in the corps command. Specifically, we were at the forward command post of the SRK in Lukavica at the Slobodan Princip Seljo barracks of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were at the forward command post in Lukavica at the Slobodan Princip Seljo barracks, can you tell us whether in this building where your service was as well, was this also the command post of General Galic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is the forward command post of the corps, which is where he was most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "where he was most of the time," can you tell us during this period of time if you can define it how much of his time did General Galic spend at the forward command post in Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: It is very hard to be precise, but I think in terms of percentages, it will be over 80 per cent. Perhaps even 90 per cent of his time. Because the situation demanded this. There were daily combat activities, and everything else that demanded for the commander to be there, although the command post was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the situation demanded this, and the daily combat activities, I'm going to ask you some questions in relation to your answer as you said about the daily combat activities. But first of all, can you tell us, did you enter the premises, the offices, of General Stanislav Galic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions. Yes, absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in your opinion, what is the view that the General had from his offices in relation to certain parts of the city of Sarajevo? Did he have a good view? What kind of view did he have?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I think I can competently answer this question because the command, that is, the office of General Galic, was located in the building that I had occupied from 1991 until the beginning of the war. So I absolutely know the positions of the offices and the premises and I know where his office was. From that office, it is practically impossible to see anything whatsoever for many reasons. The view towards Sarajevo, that is, to the part of Dobrinja and Donji Kotorac is obstructed by a building which is in the immediate vicinity, and that is the building of the soldiers' club. Furthermore, when there is a lot of greenery, a series of trees is also obstructing the view which is very near the barracks. And last but not least, because of the enemy activities and enemy fire from Dobrinja, from the direction of Dobrinja, we were forced, in order to protect our commander, we were forced to put near the barracks and between the building of the soldiers' club, we had to put concrete blocks, slabs, that were in such -- not concrete, steel slabs of such height and size that they obstructed the view towards the city. So I can say with certainty that from these premises, it was not possible to see the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence had handed over a tape that the Defence had made which is the filming of the area of the Slobodan Princip Seljo barracks, which is the forward command post of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. The actual cassette is only 1 and a half to 2 minutes long. And on this tape, you can see a certain part of that area. And with your leave, the Defence would ask if this videocassette could be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Is it available to the technicians?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is for the technical booth. And my learned colleagues have it. I had put it -- but on Friday we were in different courtrooms. I don't know whether they have it. I do have another copy here. The exhibit number is D348/7. The cassette has no sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what is this building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the building of the soldiers' club. This is the trees, the line of trees that I told you about which obstructs the view from the office of General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The video go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the top floor upstairs, to the right --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the technical booth to stop here, pause, so the witness can explain?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: From the right to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, could you please take the pointer and could you please point exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... Cannot be followed by. Can we just try that you put your questions in such a way that we know what you are talking about. What are we identifying at this moment? What would you like the witness to indicate to us, the offices of General Galic or anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If he can show us the windows of the -- General Galic's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us in which part of the building and on which floor these were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. Upstairs, on the top floor, that is, on the first floor, from the right to the left, second window, these were the windows of the office of the commander, the commander's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this building, can you see the windows of the offices where your service was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. The following window, that is the room for commander's rest, and the room after that is my own office.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness is indicating on the video material on which we can see the building of the forward command post of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the witness has just explained that the right top corner, the two windows, are the windows of General Galic's office. Going to the left, that is, to the east, the first window after that is the room for commander's rest, and then the fourth window towards the left is the office where Witness Bukva had his office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just try to clarify this. Mr. Bukva, you see on the first floor there are eight windows. You say the first two from the right-hand side were General Galic's offices. Then you said that there were a window or windows for the restroom for General Galic. Would that be the third from the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the fourth from the right, that would be your offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we now know what the four windows are that we first saw. Ms. Pilipovic, whether it's east or west, there has been no basis whatsoever to establish what is east and what is west. So you can't, just for the sake of the transcript, fill in whether it's east, west, north, or south without any basis in the testimony of the witness. Please proceed. I'm not saying it's not true, but there's no basis for it in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you tell us whether the view that we had towards the building that you told us was the soldiers' club, is this the view that would be seen from the offices -- from General Galic's office? Was that the building that you told us was the soldiers' club?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm saying that this picture was taken probably taken from one of those windows because I know this view very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you say that you know this view, in which direction in your opinion, can you tell us, regardless of the fact that you told us the soldiers' club was obstructing the view, what is the direction when we are talking about the core area and when we are talking about the Sarajevo theatre of operations, what would we be able to see if it wasn't for this soldiers' club? What would we see, could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, I think I would be able to tell you. If there were no obstructions, we would be able to see a part of Dobrinja, the airport, Donji Kotorac, and further on. This further on would mean Hrasnica, Mount Igman, and that would be that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the technical booth if they can play the videotape to the end so we can see what else is on the tape. It goes on for another minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can continue with the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop, pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you tell us, this view that we can see on the tape now, what is this area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This view, this view was filmed from the corner of the soldiers' club building, in relation to the view that I spoke of a minute ago is approximately to the 90 degrees to the right. The facility you can see on the ground on the horizon, rather, the elevation that we can see in the background, is the Mojmilo hill. And as far as the other facilities are concerned, that is, the houses that we can see, I don't think there's any point talking about this. These are private houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can now the tape be played to the end, please. I'm asking the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stop again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, for the record, we can indicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The direction you're looking in from this point, if you would use a compass, what would be the direction on the compass if you take the middle of the picture you have in front of you? Would that be north, east, west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is approximately north. Perhaps north -- more towards northeast. For instance, this tree, the thickest tree that we can see, and then the next one to the left, if we look towards that tree, that would be north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking the technical booth to continue playing the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you tell us, this area that we can see, those buildings in the background of the screen, what are they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I do not recognise those buildings. But in any case, this is Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part of Dobrinja is that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I think this is Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we now play the tape to the end, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can fast forward now, because we've already seen this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, on this video material that was played, you explained where the offices of General Galic were and yours as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I interrupt you. The Chamber is interested to see the video as a whole again because we still have some difficulties in our orientation. And perhaps you could tell us a bit more about also the -- I mean, sometimes I see it's zoomed in. Is that from the same camera position? I do understand that the first pictures were, as the witness told us, from the window of the office of General Galic. That would have been more clear to us if that would have been known to us right away. But perhaps we could see the video in its entirety once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, of course. What I just wanted to say is that the second part was filmed from the corner of the building as the witness explained. There are perhaps some parts that were zoomed, and you can see Mojmilo and Igman, but we can have a look at the tape again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For example, if the witness would indicate when he sees Igman, because Mojmilo I think was clear. Igman was not mentioned as far as I know until now, so we would like to get as much information from the video as possible. So let's play it again. When you see Mount Igman, could you please ask to stop just perhaps by using the word "stop," and then you indicate where you see Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness -- or rather, Your Honour, with your leave I was going to just help. The communication, the road, where the cars are going, what is this road? Where is it going?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the road Lukavica-Vojkovici, and then further on Srpsko Trnovo and so on. I have to say that it is probable that we will not be able to see Mount Igman here precisely from the position that the first scenes were filmed in the background, that's where Igman is. But probably because of the quality of the filming it's not possible to actually see Igman. So from the windows of my office, that is, from the window of the office of my commander, it is possible to see Igman very well. But here it is impossible because of the angle and the lighting during the filming.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is good. I apologise. So after all, in the background behind the facilities, it is possible to see the contours of Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, from the camera point of view where you have told us that you see some structures in Dobrinja IV and Igman in the background, what would be the direction the camera is facing at this moment? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, this is the direction which is parallel to the view from the office of my commander and myself. I presume that the camera was located exactly at the corner of the command building, so we can say that this is a parallel view with a slight difference. So this will be slightly different from the view that would be seen from the office of the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you for the direction the camera is pointing at. Because a view usually gives an angle of, well, let's say, from east to south 90 degrees or more, up to 180 degrees. But what would be the direction you look here from the building which, as you tell us, is approximately the same as from the window of General Galic's offices? Would this be northwest or...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if we can geographically give directions, this would be more to the west, except that it is possible that it is slightly northwest. But in any case, it's west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bukva, considering that we were able to see the positions of Igman and Mojmilo, in your opinion, considering that you lived in Sarajevo, strategically speaking, the positions of Igman and Mojmilo, in relation to Sarajevo proper or to the most of Sarajevo, how would you qualify those positions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: These are very important positions, and from the point of view of the military, they represent an advantage for the side that would have control of those. In relation to the SRK forces, these positions were extremely important and represented a high-risk area for the SRK forces because these positions were under the control of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, on the video, when you saw the premises of the general as well as yours, can you tell us whether in this building meetings were held of the corps command and where in this building the meetings you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you to enter a new area about meetings rather than the geographical position of the barracks. We have got two minutes left before the break. Would you please instruct the witness as to what to mark on the maps. I noticed that according to the transcript, you asked him to mark workshops, military positions, and areas where weapons used by the BH army. That's quite a task, I think. I don't know whether you want all military positions or headquarters or confrontation lines or whatever. But could you please give clear instructions to the witness what to mark.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind that this is a lot of work, the witness -- the Defence wanted the witness to mark the locations, precise locations, that he knew about where the troops of the 1st Corps of the BH army were located. That is, command posts of the units that he knows about. And if this is also appropriate, we wanted the witness to mark the command posts and if he can also make a key for this map, with your leave, and also for the workshop if he can put the letter R marking the workshops. And also, if he has any knowledge about the positions of weapons, he can put the letter O for weapons or letter N for weapons. For command posts, he can put the KM for command posts. For us, that would be enough. And on the map, we could see where the command posts were, where the workshops, were and where the weapons positions were. And he can also put heavy weapons positions, TN, TN for heavy weapons. And for command posts, KM. And for workshops, R.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also suggested --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless you have a better proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Weapons in general, but would you like to limit your request to heavy weapons, or would you like heavy depots as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness knows about the warehouses, weapons warehouses, then he could also mark that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were asked, and I am aware that I am asking a lot of you because where we have a break, we'll ask you to work. Of course, if you need a break as well, you can take some break as well. But during this half hour, if you could mark with an R any location of workshops where weapons or ammunition was manufactured; with an O, any warehouses or concentration of weapons; with a KM any command post you would know, and perhaps then later on we'll find out what kind of command posts these were; and TN for where heavy weapons were located. If you would like to write it down, but otherwise you'll certainly be assisted by -- if you have forgotten about the letters to use. We'll then adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The break has taken a bit more time, but it's also due to the time the witness used to prepare his markings. Where do we stand as far as the markings are concerned? Could it be -- could they be put on the ELMO, and have the parties had an opportunity to look at the markings made by the witness, or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we perhaps zoom in on the markings made by the witness so we are better able to... Ms. Pilipovic, could you guide the witness through the markings he made.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, could you first of all tell us, the positions that you have marked in, which part of the town are they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the Cengic Vila part of town, and Alipasino Polje, Alipasin bridge, Svrakino Selo, Alipasino Polje, and Svrakino village. And up here, there is Buljakov stream and Boljakov stream.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which point of the compass is this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the northern part of the town. It's the north. It's in this direction. It's towards the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think the general aspects of the map are sufficiently known to the Chamber, not to be of specific attention unless there would be need in order to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you tell us which positions you have marked and what these markings mean. You could start with the first position which has been marked with the letters TN.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: To the north, TN, that's the Zlatiste garbage dump location. The heavy artillery was located there. Howitzer battery, 155 millimetre Howitzer and 120 millimetre mortar battery from the 112th Vitez Motorised Brigade. It's command post you can see has been marked here. Its the command post of the 112th --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm afraid we might have to go over that last part because I didn't see what he was pointing to. The monitor focussed on the courtroom, not on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, perhaps what we could do is to zoom in always on the relevant part the witness is pointing at. So I think the first part was explained sufficiently, Mr. Stamp, that that's the location indicated by TN. And I take it that copies will be made of the marked map soon so that.... So then the next one, you pointed at the headquarters. Could you point at it so that we zoom in then on the headquarters you indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the ELMO zoom in to where the witness points at. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, can you tell us about the positions, about the other markings. What do they indicate on the map, the ones that we can see to the left of the place which you have marked with the command post of the 112th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the command post of the 102nd Infantry Mountain Brigade. This was located in Zica factory, in the wire factory. One of the battalions of this brigade was in the Pavle Goranin primary school. That's this position here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness now points at a place where attached to it it's written Skola Pavle Goranin. I think it is approximately just above the word Novi Grad on the map. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, let's return to the upper part of the map. The 102nd Motorised Brigade, which is to the left with regard to the 112th, can you just move the map to the left and have a look at the left-hand corner. It says MAD, 102 KM?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is a mixed artillery battalion of the 102nd Infantry Brigade. This is its command post and its firing position which were located behind the Solitar Bosna Montaza building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the mixed artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Battalion, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you knew what weapons this mixed artillery battalion possessed.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: As in the case of the 112th Brigade, it had 105-millimetre Howitzer battery or 155-millimetre Howitzer battery, and 120-millimetre mortar battery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have now marked this and explained that --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: We have another part of this brigade's combat position. It's the mixed anti-armour artillery battalion, which was located in the Dzemala Bijedica Street. At the very beginning of that street. Its position was across the road from the Slon car wash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness now points at a marking which is triangular shape of which the basis is where the map reads "Cengic Vila." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, in this battalion, did you know what sort of armour the mixed anti-armour artillery battalion possessed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the time of the war, the period of the war. The battalion had some anti-armour weapons, mostly Maljutkas. But in 1993, this battalion also had an anti-armour system called the red arrow. It was of American production. We know this for a fact because some of our anti-armour equipment had been hit by the system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner, above this, you have the number 111, and it says KM. Could you tell us something about this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: If you will just allow me to say the following, that's the command post of the 111th Infantry Brigade which was located in the former building of Bosnalijek in the Blagoje Parovica Street. That street is now called Paromlinska in this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness points at where the eastern and the western part of the map are connected, where the basis of the marking is on the eastern part of the map and whereas the flag appears on the western part of the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, can you show us the other part of the plan where you have marked the command posts of certain units. And can you use the plan to tell us about the command post that you have marked in this part of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, but it would more difficult to start with the 1st Corps as an operational unit of the BH army. Its position was here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The best way of proceeding that you indicate what marking you'd like to be described by the witness so that you say "I draw to your attention to the marking there and there, please point at it." If you describe it first, and then ask the witness what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, you've marked with the letters 1K in a rectangle, and below we have the letters KM. And to the right of that rectangle, there is a little triangle. Can you tell us what this marking indicates?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: It indicates the command post of the 1st BH army corps which was in Danijela Ozme Street number 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which building the command post was located in, the Danijela Ozme Street number 7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think counsel spoke of a triangle to the right of a square when the witness was pointing to one adjoining and below the square. I don't know which one the record should appropriately reflect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was my understanding that counsel was pointing at a triangular-shaped part of a marking which is attached to the letters KTC, I think it is, and then 100/112. Then please proceed. I see that counsel confirms this by nodding. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But maybe we should clarify that with the witness. The witness is not nodding. What I am indicating to the Court is that counsel refers to one thing and the witness appears to be pointing to another another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact the witness was explaining to us what was the meaning of the marking, the rectangular flag 1.K, and that counsel just by way of reference pointed at the triangular shape which is not part of the marking the witness is explaining to us. Is that correct, Ms. Pilipovic? And do I understand this to be your understanding as well, Mr. Bukva?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The triangle that you have spoken about and which indicates the command post of the 1st Corps, is it connected to this flag above?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I think that this can be seen very clearly. There is a triangle and a flag is attached to it, and it says 1.K on the flag. And this triangle here indicates the exact position of the command of the 1st Corps. So this is whole, this flag and this triangle constitute a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the witness is now pointing at a small triangle which is the basis of the pole of the flag containing 1.K. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, I asked you whether you knew which building the command of the 1st Corps was located in.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: It was a residential building which was across the road from the presidency. And behind the building in which Jugo Banka was located. It was in Danijela Ozme Street, number 7, Danijela Ozme street, a residential building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many floors that residential building had?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't be precise, but I don't think that it had more than six floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know which floor the command post was located on?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Mostly on the ground floor, but the command organs also used certain flats for rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you have marked the map with a triangle which has a flag where it says "105 PBR." And below that it says KM?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's this. It's the 105th Infantry Brigade which was located in the Sipad building in Trampina Street. To the left you can see a park and the street where the command post of the 105th Infantry Brigade was located was there, it was in the Sipad building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say in the Sipad building, was that -- were those business premises or were the Sipad premises within some sort of other building? Can you tell us whether this Sipad building was a separate building or was it part of some other building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it's a separate building. And the premises concerned were business premises, but it was in a part of the town which was fairly densely inhabited. There were quite a few buildings surrounding it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bukva, between these two markings, there is a circle, there is a triangular flag on it, and you have marked this with the letters KM, 100/112.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I have to correct you. I apologise. This IDO/112. It can't be very clearly seen on the map. It says IDO/112.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this circle with the triangular flag where it says KM, IDO/112. Is this one single marking?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the combat position of the 112th Vitez Motorised Brigade, and this is a reconnaissance and sabotage detachment, that's what IDO stands for, which was located in the Danijela Ozme Street number 2 in the Jugo Banka building. It's right across the road from the presidency building. This is -- this reconnaissance and sabotage detachment had about 140 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I've understood you correctly, you said it was part of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: The 112th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 112th Brigade. Mr. Bukva, can you tell us what the triangle is which has an arrow which points towards the south. There is also a flag where it says GS, with a diacritic mark, and KM. Can you tell us something about this.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the command post of the main staff of the BH army. It was located in the presidency building, in the basement of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the left, there's a triangle which has a flag, in which it says 1KM 102.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Again, a slight correction. This is IKM 102. This is the forward command post of the 102nd Infantry Brigade which was located in the Valter Peric buildings. The triangle indicates those buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the Valter Peric buildings, can you be a little more specific and tell us what sort of buildings are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: These are the business premises of the BH electricity supply network. They are in the vicinity of Skenderija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bukva. Could you please move the map on the ELMO so we can see the parts we have not yet seen. Tell us about the triangle with the flag in which it says 115th PBR, KM?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the command post of the 115th Infantry Brigade which was located in Bistrik in the buildings of the former command of the JNA, of the former JNA 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to that marking, we can see a circle in which there is the letter R. Can you tell us what R stands for. I have seen it elsewhere, too.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This circle indicates the brewery buildings in which weapons and ammunition workshop was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right, we have a circle in which there is the letter N.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This circle indicates the tunnel at the main road from Sarajevo to Pale above Bembasa in which there was a warehouse of ammunition and other equipment of the BH army. I think this warehouse was under the direct control and command of the main staff of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Above and to the right, we can see a triangle with a flag in which it says "152 PBR" and below, the letters KM.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to clarify something. I have to point out that the map hasn't -- doesn't include the barracks of the former JNA, the so called Jajce barracks, but I have marked it here. So it's perhaps a little further to the right here, the barracks of the former JNA. The Jajce barracks is a barracks in which the command post of the 152nd Infantry Brigade was located. And a significant part of that brigade was located in that barracks, was billeted in that barracks. Out of the equipment in the barracks itself, they had two 105-millimetre Howitzers, and two 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map, we can see a circle and there is a triangular flag attached to it and it says 1-115 in the flag and there's a primary school below it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to clarify something. We had the 115th Brigade here in Bistrik, and one of its battalions, this is 1-115. One of it's battalions was in the primary school in the part of town called Hrid [phoen]. This was here, at this crossroads here. And that's where the Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 18350 to 18358. primary school was located. So all the men that were part of this battalion were billeted in this primary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the map just be moved a bit upwards so that we can -- no, a bit to the down so that... Yes. Is that -- words written, is that B/C/S for primary school? Skola, I do recognise, but not the first word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Osnovni, which means primary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, as far as I can see, in the right part of the map, you have explained -- you have told us about all the markings you have made in the right part of the map as far as I have been able to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: I apologise. There is a part that we have skipped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us about it. The letter R, and I can see a circle, too.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. That's at the corner where the tram turns towards the railway station. It's the central technical engineering school. And weapons and ammunition warehouse, workshop, was also located there. We haven't mentioned this part either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The circle with the letter N --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, for the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed at an R which is at the beginning of the word Marin Dvor. And I think the next location the witness intended to point at is to the N in a circle just left of the R I mentioned a second ago. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have mentioned this circle and the letter N inscribed in the circle. Can you tell us about this building? Does it have anything to do with this circle and the letter N?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You can see that it's the Marshal Tito barracks, the former JNA barracks. That's the complex here. Here we have the buildings, and here at the corner, we had the logistics part of the main staff of the BH army. Weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, other military equipment, was located here. That's in the right part of the barracks, whereas in the left part of the barracks, there was the Ukrainian battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The triangle with the little flag where it says Guard's Brigade and KM below, what does this indicate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This triangle with the flag indicates the command post of the Guard's Brigade, which was attached to the main staff of the BH army. It was a unit attached to the main staff of the BH army, and it was billeted in this right part of the Marshal Tito barracks, just like the logistics section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, the triangle with a flag in which it says "1 KM" and 102 below, what does that indicate and where was it located?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: We've spoken about this already. It's the Valter Peric forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I have understood you, you have told us about the right part of the map. I think that you haven't mentioned something in the left part of the map, the letter R that we can see in a circle below the word Nikolici?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is a weapons and ammunition workshop located in the factory of optical science.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The lower part of the map, I've also noticed that there are two markings in this part. There are circles in which we have the letter R.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is also a weapons and ammunition workshop which was in Dzemala Bijedica Street, number 144. It was located in the building of the Astra factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the left, we can also see the letter R in the circle.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes. It has to do with the same thing. Factory of weapons and ammunition, and it was in the Zica factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, if you can just show us the part of the map which I believe we haven't seen yet, which is the area of Dobrinja. There is a symbol of a triangle with the flag where it says 155 PBV, and below, there's KM, if I am reading it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: This is the command post of the 155th Infantry Brigade. This command post was located at the Mitsubishi Avenue. I think it was in the Sipad building. That's approximately here. And this brigade was commanded by Ismet Hadzic. He used to live at the October Revolution Street, and he also had a company of military police within his brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can also see a smaller circle in this area, with a KM and a smaller flag, and I don't know what you've written here above is in relation to this symbol, to this circle. Or does it mean anything else so that we avoid any confusion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, this is in relation to the circle with the triangle flag, and it says KM, battalion Djerzelez. And this command post was at the kindergarten, the building of the kindergarten on this location. Command post of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bukva, considering that you have a better overview of both parts of the map of Sarajevo, can you tell us whether you have clarified for us all locations that you marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BUKVA
utterances.text: Yes, I think we've clarified all locations, except I'd like to offer one other comment in relation to 155th Infantry Battalion. Apart from the Djerzelez battalion, which was the assault and manoeuvre force of this brigade, under the direct command of this brigade, there was another battalion called El Fatah. And this battalion was composed of mujahedins, of mujahedin only. And the command post of that battalion, I did not mark it because it was frequently changed. It was -- this battalion was very frequently in combat operations. And it wasn't stationed in Dobrinja all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
